substantive_reconstruction.degree_and_indices: The leading term of (1-t)^(k+1) is (-1)^(k+1)t^(k+1); multiplying by t^i gives degree i+k+1 with nonzero leading coefficient (-1)^(k+1). Thus degree k+1 holds exactly at i=0, while i=k reaches ambient degree d=2k+1. The allowed example k=i=1 gives t-2t^2+t^3. This distinction is independent of the Bernstein basis's representation degree: a polynomial represented in degree d need not have actual degree d. Natural indices satisfy i+j<=k<=d throughout the entire j-range, hence the natural binomial denominator choose(d,i+j) is strictly positive when cast to the reals.
substantive_reconstruction.exact_elevation: Multiplying the proposed weight by B_(d,i+j) cancels precisely this nonzero binomial. Its remaining exponent is d-i-j=(k+1)+(k-i-j), so the product factors as t^i(1-t)^(k+1) choose(k-i,j)t^j(1-t)^(k-i-j). Summation is the binomial expansion of (t+(1-t))^(k-i)=1. This is an all-real polynomial identity; it neither divides by t or 1-t nor requires an interior point. At i=k only j=0 remains with weight 1/choose(d,k). At k=0 the identity is B_(1,0)=1-t; endpoint evaluations use the constant power convention and introduce no 0/0 operation.
substantive_reconstruction.actual_source_coefficients: The source coefficientSeries coefficient formula gives a_(k,i)=sum_(m=0)^i choose(k+i-m,k)/m!, nonnegative since each factorial is positive and every numerator nonnegative. Finite collection defines L_r=sum_(i,j)[r=i+j]a_i w_(i,j). These coefficients are nonnegative and vanish for r>k. I checked the full collection/evaluation proof, not only its declaration name. The reflection B_(d,r)(1-t)=B_(d,d-r)(t), including the binomial symmetry and endpoint exponents, changes F_k into coefficients L_(d-r). Therefore H_k=e^(-1)F_k+F_k(1-t) has c_r=e^(-1)L_r+L_(d-r). The positive exponential multiplies the unreflected endpoint, as the actual t=p+1 source formula requires.
substantive_reconstruction.positivity_and_grading: Coefficient nonnegativity is independent of the evaluation variable. Only the last deduction uses t in [0,1], where both endpoint powers and the binomial basis functions are nonnegative. Outside that interval the same algebraic expansion holds but its basis functions need not be nonnegative, and the answer does not assert positivity there. At k=0 the coefficient pair is (e^(-1),1) and H_0=e^(-1)(1-t)+t, confirming orientation. original_contract_fields.question: Work with the degree-d Bernstein basis B_{d,r}(t) = C(d,r) t^r (1-t)^{d-r}. For fixed k, i with i <= k, consider the single endpoint-factor monomial t^i (1-t)^{k+1} of degree k+1. Prove the exact degree-elevation identity that writes it in the degree-(2k+1) Bernstein basis: t^i (1-t)^{k+1} = sum_{j=0}^{k-i} w(k,i,j) * B_{2k+1, i+j}(t), where w(k,i,j) = C(k-i, j) / C(2k+1, i+j). Deduce that the full source polynomial has a Bernstein coefficient vector with all nonnegative entries on [0,1].

successor_contract_fields.question:
For natural numbers k and i with 0 <= i <= k, work over the real polynomial ring and define B_{d,r}(t)=C(d,r)*t^r*(1-t)^(d-r) for 0 <= r <= d. The predecessor described the endpoint-factor term t^i*(1-t)^(k+1) as having degree k+1. Is this true for every allowed i? Determine its exact degree and leading coefficient, give a counterexample to the universal description if false, and distinguish that degree from the Bernstein representation degree d=2*k+1.

Prove, for every real t, the exact identity t^i*(1-t)^(k+1)=sum_{j=0}^{k-i} w(k,i,j)*B_{d,i+j}(t), where w(k,i,j)=C(k-i,j)/C(d,i+j), with the binomial coefficients regarded as real numbers. Justify the nonzero denominators and handle i=0, i=k and k=0 without assuming t is strictly between the endpoints.

To make the same full source polynomial explicit, set a_{k,i}=sum_{m=0}^{i} C(k+i-m,k)/m! for 0 <= i <= k, F_k(t)=(1-t)^(k+1)*sum_{i=0}^{k} a_{k,i}*t^i, and H_k(t)=exp(-1)*F_k(t)+F_k(1-t). Thus H_k(t) is the source interpolant evaluated at p=t-1. Give a degree-d Bernstein coefficient formula for H_k by collecting the elevated terms and reflecting their indices. Prove its coefficients are nonnegative real numbers, and deduce H_k(t)>=0 on [0,1]. Separate the all-real exact identity from the interval restriction used for nonnegativity of the basis functions.
